#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -D /s/ls4/users/leokul01/dineof3/script
#   --ntasks 1
#   --cpus-per-task 48
#   -t 02-23:59:59
#   -p hpc4-3d
#   -o %j.out
#   -e %j.err

#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 48
#flux: --time-limit=71h59m59s

# Omitted Slurm option: -p hpc4-3d (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on different nodes than intended, affecting performance/queue time or causing policy rejection.

# Omitted Slurm options: -o/-e with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Slurm -D sets the working directory; emulate it.
cd /s/ls4/users/leokul01/dineof3/script

module load openmpi intel-compilers
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2

# Slurm used $MPIRUN; under Flux, use flux-run for launch.
# Performance implication: if your site relies on a specific mpirun/mpiexec configuration, you may need site-specific MPI settings.
flux run -n 1 -c 48 python main3_mp.py -c config/main3_default_ki_cluster.yml \
    --satellite-descriptor '../test/satellite_descriptor_ki_cluster_w3nt2.csv' \
    -S aqua \
    --logs ../test/reconstruction_logs/hooi_es_3neighbours_thresh2_aqua \
    --interpolated-stem interpolated_3neighbours_thresh2 \
    --output-stem Output_3neighbours_thresh2 \
    --decomposition-method hooi \
    --early-stopping 1

reasons: The original Slurm job constrained placement to a specific partition (`-p hpc4-3d`), but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition constraint; this can change the allocated hardware and performance characteristics (or lead to policy rejection).
